lineage_context.teaching_goal: Retain the regional/FNA Thelypteridaceae field concept for Thelypteris kunthii: terrestrial pinnate-pinnatifid fern with transparent hairs/glands and round sori usually covered by hairy reniform indusia.

taxonomy_scope.project_teaching_treatment: Retained as a separate regional/FNA teaching family because it is morphologically useful and still common in North American fern literature.
taxonomy_scope.current_kew_note: POWO 2026 treats Thelypteridaceae as a synonym within a broad Aspleniaceae and lists Thelypteris there. This is an alternative family circumscription, not a species-name conflict.

project_scope.note: The current project pool contains Thelypteris kunthii. Kew accepts the species and includes Texas in its native range, while assigning the genus to broad Aspleniaceae.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Inspect the lower surface and the frond hairs. In the regional/FNA concept, Thelypteridaceae commonly has round sori with kidney-shaped true indusia plus transparent needlelike hairs and/or glands on the frond.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Mostly terrestrial ferns with creeping to erect rhizomes. Fronds commonly 1-pinnate to pinnate-pinnatifid; transparent hairs and glands are frequent and scales are generally much less conspicuous on mature blade axes than in many other fern families.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Sori commonly round and medial to supramedial on veins; indusia often reniform/kidney-shaped, sometimes reduced or absent in other family members.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Round sorus + reniform indusium + hairy/glandular terrestrial frond is the practical regional Thelypteridaceae door.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole terrestrial frond → hairs/glands → round sori → hairy reniform indusium → vein-to-sinus pattern → broad-vs-narrow family taxonomy card
visual_lesson.intro: Thelypteris looks like a generic 'fern' until you zoom in. The lower blade is full of useful structure: hairs, glands, veins, round sori and tiny kidney-shaped indusia.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the broad terrestrial frond
steps.look_for: Large monomorphic fern with blade broadest toward the base and pinnae deeply incised toward the costa.
steps.why_it_matters: Sets it apart from the narrow black-stemmed Asplenium and small epiphytic Pleopeltis in this project batch.

steps.title: 2 · Zoom into the hairs and glands
steps.look_for: Transparent hairs on costae, veins and blade tissue, often with small stalked yellowish glands.
steps.why_it_matters: FNA uses the hairy/glandular indument as an important Thelypteridaceae character suite.

steps.title: 3 · Find a round sorus
steps.look_for: Round sori positioned roughly midway to above-midway between costa and margin.
steps.why_it_matters: Immediately separates the plant from linear-sorus Asplenium.

steps.title: 4 · Find the hairy kidney-shaped indusium
steps.look_for: A tan reniform true indusium over the sorus, often bearing short hairs in T. kunthii.
steps.why_it_matters: This is a strong reproductive tie-breaker from naked-sorus Pleopeltis and false-indusium cliffbrakes.

steps.title: 5 · Trace veins toward the sinus
steps.look_for: In T. kunthii, proximal veins from adjacent segments run toward the sinus or nearly so.
steps.why_it_matters: Adds a technical confirmation character when close Thelypteris relatives are present.

steps.title: 6 · Learn both family systems
steps.look_for: FNA/regional framework: Thelypteridaceae separate. Current Kew: Thelypteridaceae synonymized into broad Aspleniaceae.
steps.why_it_matters: Lets the crew understand why different apps, floras and databases may show different family names for the same fern.

comparisons.title: Thelypteridaceae vs Aspleniaceae (regional/FNA)
comparisons.rule: Thelypteris has round sori, commonly reniform indusia, and hairy/glandular fronds; Asplenium has linear sori with narrow one-sided indusia and clathrate stem scales.

comparisons.title: Thelypteridaceae vs Polypodiaceae
comparisons.rule: Thelypteris is terrestrial and usually has a true reniform indusium; Pleopeltis is creeping/epiphytic with peltate lower-blade scales and round sori lacking a true indusium.

comparisons.title: Thelypteridaceae vs Pteridaceae
comparisons.rule: Thelypteris sori are round and sit on the blade surface under true indusia; local cliffbrake-type Pteridaceae often has marginal sori hidden by a rolled false indusium.

visual_lesson.caveat: The family boundary is classification-dependent. The project deliberately preserves the FNA-style family as a labeled teaching unit while recording Kew's broader Aspleniaceae treatment.

genera.fast_cue: large terrestrial pinnate-pinnatifid fern + hairy/glandular underside + round sori + hairy reniform indusia

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Species accepted by current Kew and FNA.
Kew treats Thelypteridaceae as a family synonym of broad Aspleniaceae; FNA retains Thelypteridaceae separately. Project keeps both frameworks explicit.
